title: Short Stuff: Whisky or Bourbon?
summary: Short Stuff episode explaining the differences between whiskey, bourbon, and Tennessee whiskey. The hosts define whiskey (grain spirit distilled below 190 proof, aged in oak), American straight whiskey (aged in new charred oak for at least two years, made in one state), and bourbon (corn-based, distilled at 160 proof or below, entered barrels at 125 proof or below per the hosts' figure of 140 corrected, aged in new charred oak). They note bourbon can be made anywhere in the US, not only Kentucky, and that Congress declared bourbon "America's native spirit." Jack Daniel's is discussed as a Tennessee whiskey that qualifies as bourbon but adds the Lincoln County process of charcoal mellowing. The episode also covers Jack Daniel's yeast mother culture and the claim that women tend to prefer higher-proof whiskeys, and ends with hosts' personal drinking preferences.

segments.title: What whiskey is and American whiskey rules
segments.summary: Whiskey is defined as a grain spirit distilled below 190 proof and aged in oak. American whiskey is regulated by the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau. American straight whiskey must be aged in new charred oak for at least two years and be made in one state.
topics: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau

segments.title: Bourbon rules and geography
segments.summary: Bourbon must be corn-based, distilled at 160 proof or below, entered into barrels at lower proof, and aged in new charred oak. Bourbon can be made anywhere in the US, not only Kentucky, and Congress declared it America's native spirit.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Short ad break before the Tennessee whiskey segment.

segments.title: Tennessee whiskey and the Lincoln County process
segments.summary: Jack Daniel's is a Tennessee whiskey that follows bourbon process and qualifies as bourbon, but adds charcoal mellowing (the Lincoln County process), filtering the unaged spirit through maple charcoal made from burned maplewood logs. The whiskey is brown from the charred oak aging, not the charcoal.

segments.title: Yeast and flavor differences
segments.summary: Flavor differences come from ingredients and yeast. Jack Daniel's uses a mother culture said to date back to Prohibition, grown daily in its lab. The hosts also note that a claim says women tend to prefer higher-proof whiskeys, attributed to Carrie Richardson of the Bourbon Women's Association in Louisville.

segments.title: Hosts' whiskey preferences
segments.summary: Hosts discuss whether they prefer firewater or smooth whiskey, and Chuck describes drinking it at a show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and give the iHeartRadio and HowStuffWorks credit.
